jobs.prompt: Two owner bugs from atlas. (1) The hand-build guard (tools/handbuild.mjs guardDecision, tools/self-approval.mjs, tools/shell-writes.mjs, tools/handbuild-guard.mjs) refuses even a swarm change preview from the orchestrator session. A preview is swarm change REASON [FILE] WITHOUT --yes: it only prints what the change order would cancel, reopen and need (read-only) and must be ALLOWED in every invocation form the guard already handles (plain, with --root, cd prefix, node runner form, quoted reasons containing words like approve or approved). The recording form with --yes stays refused for an agent session exactly as today (owner or policy only). Find the exact rule that blocks the preview, fix it narrowly, make the refusal message for --yes name the rule id and say that the preview is allowed. (2) Policy: small change orders that only rename a file inside an already approved requirement must be auto-approved by the policy engine instead of needing the owner. Add a pure module tools/change-order-class.mjs exporting classifyChangeOrder(oldScopeText, newScopeText) returning { renameOnly, renames: [{from,to}], addedRequirements, removedRequirements, changedRequirements, reasons }: renameOnly is true only when requirements are neither added nor removed, every changed line pair differs only in file-path-looking tokens (same number of tokens, same words around them, each differing token a path with a file extension or a directory prefix), at least one rename exists, and at most 5 renames. Add a standing rule change-order-rename-only to tools/policy.mjs (kind change-order, conditional like the existing commit-window rule, fail closed): auto-approve when facts.renameOnly is exactly true, facts.addedRequirements and removedRequirements are 0, facts.cancelsTickets and facts.reopensTickets are 0, renames count between 1 and 5, no renamed path is a protected path (coordination/checks.json, .project-swarm.json, workflows under .github, package files, secrets-looking paths) and the project already has an approved ledger; log rule id and renames in the auto-decision log before applying (as the engine does); anything else stays with the owner. swarm policy check change-order --facts JSON must decide it; list the rule in swarm policy show and docs/policy.md. Do NOT edit tools/scope-commands.mjs (another seat owns it): write the exact wiring hook (function name and one example call) into the header comment of tools/change-order-class.mjs. Tests: tests/guard-change-preview.test.mjs (preview allowed in all forms through guardDecision and the hook script; --yes refused with rule id), tests/change-order-class.test.mjs and tests/policy-change-order.test.mjs (rename-only true and false cases: added requirement, reworded sentence, path with different directory depth plus extra words, six renames, a protected path, cancelled tickets; no policy file means nothing auto-approved). Keep the existing guard and policy tests passing (run every test file with handbuild, guard, self-approval, shell-writes or policy in the name). ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.
